A NOTE ON READING THIS MAP

A world of histories.

This is a curated atlas of societies, states, and cultural traditions across 4,700 years. Each date reveals a historical chapter, alongside other societies living at the same time.

Places, not precise borders

Markers indicate representative cities or regions. Soft halos help locate them; their size does not encode territory, population, or importance. Modern coastlines are a geographic reference. Capital locations can shift between chapters.

A sample, not the whole world

Blank areas do not mean nobody lived there. “Civilization” is an accessible umbrella term here, never a ranking. Some entries are states; others cover many distinct communities. A record’s endpoint usually marks political change, not the disappearance of a people. Entries marked “continues” extend beyond 1700.

How time works

BCE counts backward; CE counts forward, with no year zero. Ancient dates and period boundaries are often approximate or debated. Text describes the broader period containing your selected year, not an event in every individual year. Chronology labels on the slider are navigation aids, not universal stages of development. The small bars count entries in this curated atlas, not population or all societies in existence.

Sources & credits

Original short summaries draw on museum, heritage, university, and historical reference materials. Open “Read the source” in any civilization’s story. Historical research reviewed September 2026.

The Met’s Timeline of Art History ↗UNESCO World Heritage Centre ↗World History Encyclopedia ↗National Museum of Australia ↗Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa ↗

Geography: Natural Earth, public domain, via world-atlas. Rendering: D3 and TopoJSON, ISC. Typography: Fraunces and DM Sans, SIL Open Font License. All runtime assets are included in this page; it works offline. No analytics.
